title: The Association of Standardized Patient Educators Standards of Best Practice
key_extraction: Cases should align with measurable objectives; be authentic and repeatable; include history affect symptoms and cues; undergo review and dry-runs
design_implication: Treat disclosure policy and cue timing as assessable case components with expert review and pilot testing
limitations: Consensus standard; does not prescribe a universal turn-level taxonomy

title: ASPE Case Development Template
key_extraction: Comprehensive case-development structure built on ASPE standards
design_implication: Use as a completeness checklist rather than copying the template
limitations: Copyrighted; educational-use terms require attribution and restrict commercial reuse

title: Healthcare Simulation Standards of Best Practice Simulation Design
key_extraction: Simulation design should be objective-aligned systematic piloted and evaluated
design_implication: Disclosure behaviors need explicit objectives prebriefing assumptions pilot scenarios and evaluation criteria
limitations: Broad simulation standard; not specific to conversational disclosure

title: Minimum standards and development perspectives for the use of simulated patients
key_extraction: Case development and SP training require quality standards and structured processes
design_implication: Add governance training-equivalent documentation and quality review to AI-SP authoring
limitations: Position paper; jurisdiction differs from Korean CPX

title: A Practical Approach to Developing Cases for Standardized Patients
key_extraction: Guidelines governing what the SP discloses to the learner improve case value
design_implication: Represent disclosure instructions separately from medical truth
limitations: Older practice article; full text availability and methods need database verification

title: Standardized Patients Part 2 Developing a Case
key_extraction: A secondary-hosted full copy describes opening statements as a case element
design_implication: Opening behavior may need explicit case-level authoring
limitations: Athletic-training context; authorized primary full-text appraisal remains pending

title: Developing standardized patient-based cases for communication training
key_extraction: Cases benefit from iterative multidisciplinary development attention to emotion stereotypes and pilot revision
design_implication: Require clinical communication and SP-methodology review rather than model-only authoring
limitations: Specific to diagnostic-uncertainty communication cases

title: Guidelines for the Development of Objective Structured Clinical Examination Cases
key_extraction: A secondary-hosted copy appears to describe case-specific opening statements conditional release and cue timing
design_implication: Opening and patient prompts may need case-configurable timing
limitations: Substantive final extraction awaits an authorized original or lawful library copy; do not redistribute the secondary copy

title: Human Simulation Program Policy and Procedure Handbook
key_extraction: Some information must not be offered unless asked; reasonable questions should receive enough information; unspecified facts should not be ad-libbed
design_implication: Implement prompted-only facts bounded sufficiency and explicit unknown responses
limitations: Operational guidance rather than comparative empirical research

title: The Objective Structured Clinical Examination AMEE Guide No 81 Part II
key_extraction: Complex roles require advance training to ensure reliable repeated portrayal across candidates
design_implication: Provider and run-to-run behavior must be evaluated for repeatability
limitations: Organization and administration focus; detailed disclosure rules not central

title: Training framework for high-stakes OSCE
key_extraction: Script work mock videos feedback and readiness checks target complete role accuracy
design_implication: Create gold trajectories and readiness thresholds before deployment
limitations: Single-program experience; not an LLM study

title: The Advantages and Challenges of Unannounced Standardized Patients Methodology
key_extraction: SPs followed physician lead and varied disclosure with open versus closed questions; fidelity tracked prompted volunteered omitted and withheld facts
design_implication: Evaluate each fact by elicitation status and distinguish open-question bundles from focused answers
limitations: Small role-specific sample; unannounced clinical setting

title: Standardized Patients in Medical Education A Review of the Literature
key_extraction: SP education has broad evidence but heterogeneous methods and outcomes
design_implication: Use for background and citation chasing rather than turn-level rules
limitations: Descriptive review; limited direct evidence for disclosure timing

title: Development of a standardized role script template for simulated participant scenarios in the German-speaking countries
key_extraction: A 19-member working group ran a Delphi-based process over 10 rounds with a systematic literature review a 24-member interprofessional expert panel and 11 reviews by experienced simulated participants and produced a modular 13-category interprofessional role script template because institution-specific scripts were not interchangeable
design_implication: A CPX v5 case policy should be a reviewable modular script artifact validated by SP-methodology experts rather than a locally invented field set; template usability itself is still pending evaluation
limitations: German-speaking interprofessional context; the template's usability and ongoing development are explicitly stated as future work; abstract-level appraisal and no turn-level disclosure algorithm

title: Who Am I and Why Am I Here A Scoping Review Exploring the Templates and Protocols That Direct Actors in Their Roles as Simulated Standardized Patients
key_extraction: A PRISMA-ScR-guided search of Embase Classic plus Embase ProQuest ERIC Ovid MEDLINE Ovid EMCare psycINFO and Scopus included 17 articles describing templates or protocols intended to let simulated patients adopt roles accurately and consistently; the located templates differed in structure length and depth across medical nursing allied health and veterinary disciplines and reporting quality was appraised with the Simulation Research Rubric
design_implication: Confirms that an explicit role template or protocol is the established mechanism for accurate and consistent SP portrayal while also confirming that no single template structure is standardized; CPX v5 must author its own reviewable template and justify its structure rather than cite an existing standard
limitations: Scoping review reporting heterogeneity rather than prescribing one template; does not define turn-level disclosure timing; abstract-level appraisal with full text pending lawful access

title: A Randomized Trial of Teaching Clinical Skills Using Virtual and Live Standardized Patients
key_extraction: Virtual and live SP performance outcomes were similar in the studied setting; standardized exposure was a benefit
design_implication: Virtual patients can support repeatable practice if interaction and content exposure are controlled
limitations: Older constrained virtual-patient technology; not free-form LLM dialogue

title: Virtual patients a critical literature review and proposed next steps
key_extraction: Virtual patients vary substantially in design and require theory-driven comparisons and clear outcomes
design_implication: Document intended learner task fidelity target and system design rather than treating all VPs as equivalent
limitations: Predates modern LLMs

title: Virtual Patient Simulations in Health Professions Education
key_extraction: Virtual-patient effectiveness is context-dependent and studies use varied comparators and outcomes
design_implication: Do not infer disclosure validity from usability or knowledge gains alone
limitations: Heterogeneous interventions; limited dialogue-specific analysis

title: Effectiveness of virtual patient tools to improve medical students clinical reasoning
key_extraction: Scaffolding debriefing reflection and human feedback can improve VP learning effectiveness
design_implication: Pair simulation with review and evidence-linked feedback; evaluate transfer separately
limitations: Clinical reasoning focus rather than patient-role fidelity

title: Training Medical Communication Skills with Virtual Patients
key_extraction: Virtual-patient communication training requires attention to interaction design realism and feedback
design_implication: Use for hypothesis generation and citation chasing
limitations: Preprint and broad review; peer-review status must be checked

title: A Language Model-Powered Simulated Patient With Automated Feedback for History Taking
key_extraction: LLM patient plus structured feedback is feasible for history-taking education
design_implication: Separate patient portrayal from assessment and validate both against human review
limitations: Prospective but limited setting and model generation

title: A large language model digital patient system enhances ophthalmology history taking skills
key_extraction: LLM digital-patient training improved measured history-taking performance in the reported setting
design_implication: Educational outcome testing is possible after fidelity is established
limitations: Specialty-specific; outcome improvement does not prove disclosure correctness

title: Embracing the Future of Medical Education With Large Language Model-Based Virtual Patients
key_extraction: The field is emerging with variable designs and limited standardized validation
design_implication: Retain explicit evidence gaps and avoid high-stakes claims
limitations: Rapidly changing evidence base and heterogeneous studies

title: Large Language Model-Based Virtual Patient Systems for History-Taking in Medical Education
key_extraction: Studies use dialogue history and few-shot prompts for gradual disclosure; common metrics include information coverage hallucination fidelity and usability
design_implication: Adopt multi-dimensional turn-level metrics and provider comparison; do not rely on one aggregate score
limitations: Included evidence varies in quality; limited multimorbidity and specialty coverage

title: Robustness of a Large Language Model-Based Virtual Patient Under Instructional Contamination
key_extraction: Premature disclosure hidden results role drift and contradictions threaten validity; forbidden leakage persisted even in clean or defended conditions
design_implication: Use forbidden-information tests prompt-injection tests and explicit claim that prompt constraints are insufficient alone
limitations: Synthetic fixed trajectories; does not establish educational effectiveness or deployment safety

title: Feasibility of Large Language Model-Based Standardized Virtual Patients in Operative Dentistry
key_extraction: Authenticity failures included taking the lead after a greeting and stating examination-only findings the patient could not know
design_implication: Test greeting behavior and epistemic access separately; action-gate examination findings
limitations: Small feasibility sample and dentistry context

title: Automated Evaluation of Standardized Patients with LLMs
key_extraction: Reliability and precision of LLM portrayals require systematic evaluation
design_implication: Use automated evaluation only with human-calibrated rubrics and evidence-linked errors
limitations: Automated judges may share model biases; conference setting

title: Human or LLM as Standardized Patients A Comparative Study for Medical Education
key_extraction: Proposes multi-agent factual consistency and expert-defined evaluation dimensions
design_implication: Consider independent consistency checks only after baseline prompt design is evaluated
limitations: Preprint; architecture should not be adopted without replication

title: Voluntary use of LLM-powered virtual standardized patients and medical students interview performance
key_extraction: Links optional VSP engagement with traditional SP assessment in an established curriculum
design_implication: Evaluate learner transfer to human-SP outcomes rather than simulator scores only
limitations: Observational association; recent online-ahead publication

title: MedSimAI Simulation and Formative Feedback Generation
key_extraction: Frames LLM simulation as deliberate practice with structured feedback
design_implication: Potential evaluation design reference; not disclosure authority
limitations: Preprint; system-specific and not direct staged-disclosure evidence

title: Clinical Performance Examination Utilizing Standardized Patients in Board Examination
key_extraction: Korean high-stakes CPX used scenario training standard videos and assessor calibration
design_implication: Korean deployment needs role training equivalence and inter-rater review
limitations: Specialty board context; limited turn-level disclosure detail

title: The Change of CPX Scores according to Repeated CPXs
key_extraction: Korean CPX assesses history communication education and integration across repeated encounters
design_implication: Supports CPX relevance and repeated practice but not a disclosure taxonomy
limitations: Indirect to patient behavior design

title: The relationship between problem-based learning and clinical performance evaluations
key_extraction: Korean CPX domains include history physical examination information sharing and patient-physician interaction
design_implication: Ensure patient behavior does not collapse distinct scored domains
limitations: Correlational educational study; indirect to staged disclosure

title: 진단·변증 스키마 기반 인공지능 표준화 환자 시스템 CURA 개발
key_extraction: Korean AI standardized-patient system uses CPX-derived data and a clinical workflow schema
design_implication: Extract Korean workflow and dialogue-design lessons after full-text appraisal
limitations: Korean-medicine context; recent source and full methods still require appraisal

title: 한의학 교육에서 내상발열 증례를 이용한 표준화환자 프로그램 개발 연구
key_extraction: Demonstrates Korean SP program development with structured history symptoms and physical findings
design_implication: Useful local case-authoring example and terminology source
limitations: Korean-medicine context; not LLM and not specifically disclosure timing

title: Introduction of a clinical skill test in the Korean Medical Licensing Examination
key_extraction: The national clinical skill test combined six CPX and six OSCE stations and used systematically trained SPs in repeated daily cycles
design_implication: Korean AI-SP pilots should preserve repeated-candidate standardization and separate interview from examination domains
limitations: Implementation report; does not expose case scripts or turn-level disclosure rules

title: Changes in the evaluation system in medical education in Korea
key_extraction: Regional Korean CPX consortia jointly developed cases and recruited and trained SPs; predetermined standardized behavior underpinned objective assessment
design_implication: Use consortium-style clinical and SP-methodology governance for case approval
limitations: Historical overview; disclosure timing is not operationalized

title: Validity and Reliability of a Clinical Performance Examination using Standardized Patients
key_extraction: A Korean nursing CPX developed scenarios and checklists and evaluated validity and reliability with 70 students
design_implication: Useful local precedent for scenario-checklist co-development and psychometric review
limitations: Nursing context and indirect to conversational disclosure

title: Clinical performance of medical students in Korea in a whole-task emergency OSCE station with a standardized patient complaining of palpitations
key_extraction: In a Korean palpitations station 150 third-year students were scored on separate history-taking physical-examination electrocardiography education and clinical-reasoning checklist items; only 18.0% checked the pulse and 38.0% never attempted an electrocardiogram
design_implication: The palpitations pilot should keep history examination investigation and education as separately observable learner actions rather than one narrative disclosure stream
limitations: Single Korean site and cohort; reports learner performance not patient disclosure behavior; abstract-level appraisal

title: Metaverse-based objective structured clinical examinations an exploratory approach to advancing clinical competency assessment
key_extraction: Korean developers integrated large language models into metaverse virtual patients for interactive history-taking while physical-examination modules were limited by absent tactile and haptic feedback
design_implication: Supports treating interviewing and examination as different capability channels in Korean assessment contexts
limitations: Exploratory development study without learner outcome or fidelity measurement; abstract-level appraisal

title: CPX_source project baseline
key_extraction: SP2B and SP2C passed for one palpitations station; SP2D.6 remains human-input-required
design_implication: Reuse accepted policy concepts cautiously; do not resume parser work implicitly
limitations: Internal evidence; one case and not external validation

title: SP2B behavior and disclosure contract
key_extraction: Forty-five policies used ask-only conditional not-disclosable spontaneous-core and open-prompted modes with truth and diagnosis firewalls
design_implication: Use as a candidate authoring vocabulary after external evidence mapping; revise opening semantics
limitations: One palpitations case; internally designed taxonomy

title: SP2C Korean utterance realization
key_extraction: Korean utterance variants were reviewed against disclosure modes
design_implication: Candidate language assets can support pilots after policy revalidation
limitations: Language set inherits SP2B opening assumptions and covers one case

title: SP2D.3 architecture comparison
key_extraction: Parser systems either over-disclosed or abstained on nearly all answerable questions; no production candidate
design_implication: Do not import deterministic semantic router into the first v5 design
limitations: Internal benchmark scope; still decisive against reusing the failed branch

title: SP2D.6 acceptance
key_extraction: All 31 adjudication rows require genuine human review before parser evaluation or SP2E
design_implication: Keep parser branch frozen; disclosure prompt work may proceed independently
limitations: Unresolved by design; not evidence that the schema is valid

title: Virtual Standardized Patient Simulation Case Development and Pilot Application to High-Value Care
key_extraction: Faculty consensus created eight cases and faculty reviewed 112 transcripts containing 4646 query-response pairs; mean avatar appropriate-response rate was 85.6%
design_implication: Use transcript-level expert ratings and report response appropriateness rather than assuming a case prompt is valid
limitations: Fourteen learners; NLP avatar predates modern LLMs; preliminary pilot

title: A GPT-Powered Chatbot as a Simulated Patient to Practice History Taking
key_extraction: Of 502 questions explicitly covered by the script 94.4% of answers used explicit script information; for 195 uncovered questions 56.4% of answers used fictitious information
design_implication: Explicitly test uncovered questions and unknown behavior; plausibility alone cannot detect invented facts
limitations: Twenty-eight students; GPT-3.5; one illness script and positive usability despite factual boundary failures

title: Enhancing Medical Interview Skills Through AI-Simulated Patient Interactions
key_extraction: AI-simulated patient practice was associated with a one-point higher mean Japanese pre-clerkship OSCE interview score and was framed as supplementary
design_implication: Measure transfer to standardized assessments but retain human simulation for nonverbal skills
limitations: Historical control; nonrandomized; educational effect does not prove disclosure fidelity

title: ECOSBot a multicenter validation pilot study
key_extraction: Across 184 sessions faculty ratings reported high authenticity correctness relevance and script coverage; communication-skill scoring agreement was weaker
design_implication: Use expert double-rating across institutions and keep patient fidelity separate from automated scoring validity
limitations: Nephrology focus; one GPT model; abstract-level appraisal

title: Development and Validation of an LLM-Based Medical History-Taking Training System
key_extraction: Three cases and 8606 learner questions were used to assess dialogue accuracy evaluation stability human-AI consistency and cross-model generalization
design_implication: Run multiple case difficulties many turns repeated scoring and cross-provider validation
limitations: Study reports aggregate accuracy; disclosure-specific error definitions require full-text appraisal

title: Feasibility of generative AI for history taking in virtual patients
key_extraction: Five experts reviewed 96 Korean-platform question-answer pairs; 2.6% of words were implausible due to inarticulate answers hallucinations or missing important information
design_implication: Include Korean expert transcript review and track hallucination omission relevance accuracy succinctness and fluency separately
limitations: One urinary case; five reviewers; Korean AI platform rather than current providers

title: GenAI-Supported Virtual Patients in Health Care Education
key_extraction: Two reviewers found 15 studies with 645 participants; evidence was heterogeneous short-duration and weakly grounded in educational theory despite promising outcomes
design_implication: Keep theory design protocol and long-term validation gaps explicit; do not generalize from feasibility
limitations: English peer-reviewed quantitative or mixed-method studies only; no meta-analysis

title: AI-powered simulated patients with automated feedback for headache history-taking
key_extraction: Twenty-five students improved OSCE and reasoning scores after repeated practice but described dialogue as sometimes robotic and limited for communication practice
design_implication: Include naturalness and communication authenticity alongside knowledge elicitation and score outcomes
limitations: Pre-post design without a contemporaneous control; three headache cases

title: Virtual standardized patient system for psychiatric interview training
key_extraction: Experienced psychiatrist scripts were refined by modified Delphi before three cases were implemented; expert evaluation reported consistency and a 20-student RCT found improved interview scores
design_implication: Require multidisciplinary script consensus before model implementation and preserve human-defined cases
limitations: Small preliminary RCT; psychiatry and ERNIE model context
